result.rule: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

result.rule: When the description states that an internal process sends information or an item to an external participant, or receives information or an item from one: Model the external participant as a separate pool and represent the stated communications with message flows.

When the description says that information is sent to an external participant and that revisions or acceptance depend on the participant’s response: Model the stated send-and-receive communications in sequence, and represent the repeated exchange with a return flow and an explicit decision about whether to continue.

When the description states that one participant’s described activity or occurrence communicates information or an item to another participant: Model the described activity or occurrence itself as the appropriate message-flow endpoint: use a task for performed work and an event for an occurrence. Do not add a separate send task merely to carry the same communication.

When the description identifies multiple external organizations as interchangeable candidates for the same interaction and says that one is selected: Model the candidates collectively as one external participant, rather than creating a separate pool and message flow for each candidate.
